title: Finite-data calculus for filtered colimits of infinity categories
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functors, cores, mapping spaces, and nested universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$ as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], filteredness and finite simplicial sets as in [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], and the infinity category $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ of $\mathcal U$-small infinity categories as modeled in [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model]. Write $\mathcal S=\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ for the infinity category of $\mathcal U$-small spaces defined in [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces]. Filtered means $\aleph_0$-filtered. Finite means having finitely many nondegenerate simplices. The infinity category $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ admits small filtered colimits and finite limits. For every small filtered infinity category $I$, finite simplicial set $K$, and coherent diagram $F:K\times I\to\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$, the canonical comparison
$$\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}\lim_{k\in K}F(k,i)\longrightarrow\lim_{k\in K}\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}F(k,i)$$
is an equivalence, including $K=\varnothing$. For every diagram $D_i\to B$ to a fixed small infinity category and every functor $T\to B$, base change also satisfies $\operatorname{colim}_i(D_i\times_B T)\simeq(\operatorname{colim}_iD_i)\times_B T$, with the structural functor from the colimit induced by the given coherent maps to $B$. The core functor $(-)^{\simeq}:\operatorname{Cat}_\infty\to\mathcal S$ and, for each finite simplicial set $L$, the functor $\operatorname{Fun}(L,-):\operatorname{Cat}_\infty\to\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ preserve small filtered colimits.

More explicitly, let $D:I\to\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ be a small filtered coherent diagram, let $C=\operatorname{colim}_I D$, and write $r_i:D_i\to C$ for its cocone. Every finite collection of objects and arrows in $C$, together with finitely many specified simplices among them, is represented up to coherent equivalence at a common stage. Given $x,y\in D_i$, the coherent coslice $I_{i/}$ of arrows out of $i$ is small and filtered, and the natural map
$$\operatorname{colim}_{(u:i\to j)\in I_{i/}}\operatorname{Map}_{D_j}(D(u)x,D(u)y)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{C}(r_ix,r_iy)$$
is an equivalence. These comparisons are natural in the objects, in precomposition and postcomposition, and under a coherent diagram of functors $D_i\to B$ to a fixed small infinity category $B$. For such a diagram and an arrow $f:p_i(x)\to p_i(y)$ in $B$, they also give the equivalence on homotopy fibers
$$\operatorname{colim}_{(u:i\to j)\in I_{i/}}\operatorname{Map}_{D_j}^{f}(D(u)x,D(u)y)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{C}^{f}(r_ix,r_iy),$$
where the superscript $f$ denotes the homotopy fiber of the map to $\operatorname{Map}_B(p_i(x),p_i(y))$. No transition functor is assumed fully faithful.

source.place: Section 3.3: finite functor-category and mapping-space calculations in the proof of Proposition 3.3.2, and finite-limit/base-change calculation in the proof of Theorem 3.3.1, using Corollary 3.3.8. Read online; not archived in literature/. These are infinity-categorical facts, not ordinary filtered colimits of sets; no Stacks tag states them.

proof.text: The marked-point model has every object cofibrant and has coherent nerve $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$. Apply the coherent-diagram model theorem to this combinatorial simplicial model. For each small shape its enriched homotopy limit and colimit, followed by the specified replacements, represent the cone and cocone universal properties in $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$. Thus this category has all small limits and colimits relative to $\mathcal U$, in particular the required finite limits and filtered colimits. Let $R$ be the complete Segal comparison. The space $R(C)_n=\operatorname{Fun}([n],C)^\simeq$ is $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Cat}_\infty}([n],C)$ by the marked mapping-space identity. Covariant representables preserve limits, so every $R(-)_n$ preserves these limits. This also identifies their actual cone legs. The equivalence $R$ detects equivalences of categories.

source.place: Section 3.3, supporting finite-data argument for Proposition 3.3.2 and Theorem 3.3.1; details below are agent-written, not a claim that the paper proves each foundational comparison.

proof.text: For $D:I\to\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$, form the pointwise space colimit $Z_n=\operatorname{colim}_I R(D_i)_n$; small space colimits exist, and the pointwise functor-category theorem assembles the faces and degeneracies coherently. For each $n\geq2$, its consecutive-edge comparison is the colimit of the Segal comparisons because the $n$-fold fiber product is a finite limit of spaces. Apply space finite-limit exactness with $\kappa=\aleph_0$ to see this comparison is an equivalence. Thus $Z$ is Segal. The equivalence-subspace lemma gives $Z_{\mathrm{eq}}\simeq\operatorname{colim}_I R(D_i)_{\mathrm{eq}}$. Completeness at each stage now gives $Z_0\simeq\operatorname{colim}_I R(D_i)_{\mathrm{eq}}\simeq Z_{\mathrm{eq}}$; the composite is the identity degeneracy, since each comparison is induced by the same degeneracy. Hence $Z$ is complete. Since the complete Segal subcategory is full, its mapping spaces from $Z$ to any complete Segal object satisfy the ambient colimit universal property. Therefore it is also a colimit there, and $R(C)\simeq Z$ with the given cocone. In particular every $R(-)_n$ preserves filtered colimits. This proves preservation of the core by taking $n=0$.

source.place: Section 3.3, supporting finite-data argument for Proposition 3.3.2 and Theorem 3.3.1; details below are agent-written, not a claim that the paper proves each foundational comparison.

proof.text: Apply $R(-)_n$ to the canonical comparison for the given $F:K\times I\to\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$. Steps 1 and 2 identify its source with $\operatorname{colim}_I\lim_K R(F(k,i))_n$ and its target with $\lim_K\operatorname{colim}_I R(F(k,i))_n$, preserving all cone and cocone maps. Space finite-limit exactness says the induced map is an equivalence for every $n$. Since $R$ is an equivalence to a full subcategory of simplicial spaces, this proves the original comparison is an equivalence. When $K=\varnothing$, the same theorem includes the filtered colimit of terminal spaces, so no nonempty-shape assumption is needed.

source.place: Section 3.3, supporting finite-data argument for Proposition 3.3.2 and Theorem 3.3.1; details below are agent-written, not a claim that the paper proves each foundational comparison.

proof.text: Every filtered indexing quasicategory is weakly contractible, and the fixed-object functor from the terminal quasicategory preserves filtered colimits. Apply the fixed-object clause to $B$ and $T$ in $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$, which admits all small colimits by step 1: their constant diagrams have colimits $B$ and $T$ with identity cocones. The given coherent arrows $D_i\to B$ and $T\to B$ form a diagram of cospans. Step 3 for the finite cospan shape therefore gives $\operatorname{colim}_I(D_i\times_B T)\simeq C\times_B T$. The induced arrow $C\to B$ is the one furnished by the original arrows and their cocone universal property. Thus the comparison is the required base-change comparison, including its structural functor.

source.place: Section 3.3, supporting finite-data argument for Proposition 3.3.2 and Theorem 3.3.1; details below are agent-written, not a claim that the paper proves each foundational comparison.

proof.text: First compute the space-valued functor $H_A(C)=\operatorname{Fun}(A,C)^\simeq$ for a finite simplicial set $A$. Use an outer induction on dimension (the empty set has dimension $-1$), and at each dimension $d\geq0$ an inner induction on the number of nondegenerate $d$-simplices. For a chosen top simplex $\sigma$, remove precisely the simplices whose unique nondegenerate ancestor is $\sigma$ to form $U\subseteq A$. This is a simplicial subset: factor any ordinal operator through its surjective and injective parts; a proper face of any other ancestor has dimension less than $d$ and cannot have ancestor $\sigma$, while an identity injective part preserves that other ancestor. Nondegenerate decomposition gives this description and shows $U$ has one fewer top simplex and all lower-dimensional simplices. The simplex gluing theorem gives $A=U\amalg_{\partial\Delta^d}\Delta^d$, allowing identified attaching faces. In every simplicial degree, maps from this pushout are pairs of maps agreeing on the boundary, so $\operatorname{Fun}(A,C)=\operatorname{Fun}(U,C)\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(\partial\Delta^d,C)}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^d,C)$. Boundary restriction on the last factor is an isofibration by exponentiation. Hence this is a homotopy pullback in $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ by the isofibration pullback theorem, and applying the core, which preserves limits by step 1 at $n=0$, makes it a homotopy pullback of spaces. For a simplex $\Delta^d$, $H_{\Delta^d}=R(-)_d$ preserves filtered colimits by step 2. For the empty set $H_{\varnothing}$ is terminal and the empty-shape space comparison gives preservation. The boundary is finite of dimension less than $d$, so its assertion is available by the outer induction even if its faces identify in $A$; the assertion for $U$ is available by the inner induction, or the outer induction if no top simplices remain. Space finite-limit exactness therefore gives preservation for $H_A$ and completes both inductions. No assumption that $A$ is a quasicategory is used.

source.place: Section 3.3, supporting finite-data argument for Proposition 3.3.2 and Theorem 3.3.1; details below are agent-written, not a claim that the paper proves each foundational comparison.

proof.text: For $L=\varnothing$, the functor $\operatorname{Fun}(L,-)$ is constant at the terminal category and preserves filtered colimits by step 4. For nonempty finite $L$, examine the canonical map $\operatorname{colim}_I\operatorname{Fun}(L,D_i)\to\operatorname{Fun}(L,C)$ after applying $R(-)_n$. By step 2 its source becomes $\operatorname{colim}_I\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^n\times L,D_i)^\simeq$, and the target is $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^n\times L,C)^\simeq$, using the exponential identity from the definition of internal functor simplicial sets. The product $\Delta^n\times L$ is finite: each nondegenerate product simplex has dimension at most $n+\dim L$, since in greater dimension its two coordinates have a common degeneracy, and there are finitely many possibilities in each of the remaining degrees. Step 5 says this map is an equivalence. The comparisons respect precomposition with every simplex operator; equivalence detection by $R$ proves preservation by $\operatorname{Fun}(L,-)$.

source.place: Section 3.3, supporting finite-data argument for Proposition 3.3.2 and Theorem 3.3.1; details below are agent-written, not a claim that the paper proves each foundational comparison.

proof.text: For a small coherent diagram of spaces $S:I\to\mathcal S$, its colimit components are the ordinary colimit of the sets $\pi_0S_i$ over the homotopy category $hI$: a map from a space to a discrete set is exactly a function on its path components; the space of such maps is discrete. Thus the cocone universal property, tested against every discrete set, identifies the two sets, since all higher compatibility choices into a discrete set are unique. The category $hI$ is ordinary filtered: nonemptiness and common successors follow by coning the empty and two-vertex shapes, and any parallel pair is coequalized in $hI$ by a cone on its finite two-edge shape. Consequently a component of $\operatorname{colim}_I S_i$ has a representative in some $S_i$, and representatives of finitely many components have a common stage. Explicitly, the ordinary colimit is the disjoint union of the $\pi_0S_i$ modulo the equivalence relation generated by transition identifications; any finite chain of those identifications is moved to a common successor using filteredness. This argument is only about components, not a replacement of homotopy colimits by ordinary set colimits.

source.place: Section 3.3, supporting finite-data argument for Proposition 3.3.2 and Theorem 3.3.1; details below are agent-written, not a claim that the paper proves each foundational comparison.

proof.text: The objects, arrows and specified simplices in the finite collection generate a finite simplicial subset $L$ of $C$ (take their faces and degeneracies; only finitely many nondegenerate faces occur). The inclusion is an object of $\operatorname{Fun}(L,C)$. Steps 5 and 7 applied to $H_L$ show that its component comes from some $\operatorname{Fun}(L,D_i)^\simeq$. A path in this core is precisely a coherent equivalence of these diagrams, so the resulting $L\to D_i$ represents all of the prescribed data simultaneously up to coherent equivalence. Multiple finite collections may equally be joined as a finite disjoint union. The case with no prescribed data is covered by nonemptiness of $I$.

source.place: Section 3.3, supporting finite-data argument for Proposition 3.3.2 and Theorem 3.3.1; details below are agent-written, not a claim that the paper proves each foundational comparison.

proof.text: Fix $i$ and let $J=I_{i/}$, with vertex projection $q:J\to I$. The cocone-category filteredness theorem applied to the one-vertex diagram $i$ makes $J$ filtered; its simplicial sets are small, being constructed from the small $I$ by the arrow/coslice construction. For any $a\in I$, apply the object-and-morphism description in the comma criterion to $q$: an object of $J\times^h_I I_{a/}$ is an object $(u:i\to j)$ of $J$ together with an arrow $v:a\to q(u)=j$. A morphism is an arrow between the common vertices together with both commuting triangles; higher simplices specify the compatibilities of both triangles. These are exactly the objects, morphisms and higher simplices of the coherent cocone category on the finite discrete diagram $\{i,a\}$. Thus this comma category is filtered by the cocone-category theorem and weakly contractible by the filtered-contractibility theorem. The coherent comma criterion therefore proves $q$ cofinal, preserving the actual cocone. Hence $\operatorname{colim}_J D(q(-))\simeq C$ and the same restriction preserves the space colimits in step 2.

source.place: Section 3.3, supporting finite-data argument for Proposition 3.3.2 and Theorem 3.3.1; details below are agent-written, not a claim that the paper proves each foundational comparison.

proof.text: For $u:i\to j$ in $J$ use the two coherently transported vertices $D(u)x,D(u)y$. They define a coherent point over $R(D_j)_0^2$. The complete Segal mapping-space comparison identifies $\operatorname{Map}_{D_j}(D(u)x,D(u)y)$ with the homotopy fiber of $R(D_j)_1\to R(D_j)_0^2$ at this point. Take the filtered colimit of these homotopy pullbacks over $J$. Space finite-limit exactness and its empty-shape clause identify the colimit of the point diagrams with a point and the resulting square with the homotopy fiber of $R(C)_1\to R(C)_0^2$ at $(r_ix,r_iy)$, using step 9 and preservation of the $R$ levels. This is $\operatorname{Map}_C(r_ix,r_iy)$. The map is induced by the cocone on arrows, so it is exactly the displayed comparison. Naturality in the objects follows from the natural mapping-fiber comparison. For composition, use $R(D_j)_2\simeq R(D_j)_1\times_{R(D_j)_0}R(D_j)_1$: $d_1$ gives composition, the outer faces give the two factors, and the degeneracy gives the identity. Preservation of these levels and face maps makes this same calculation commute with precomposition and postcomposition. In every higher degree the same simplicial operators are retained, so the comparison respects their coherent associativity and all higher compositions as well.

source.place: Section 3.3, supporting finite-data argument for Proposition 3.3.2 and Theorem 3.3.1; details below are agent-written, not a claim that the paper proves each foundational comparison.

proof.text: For a coherent transformation $p:D\to\Delta_I B$, apply $R$ to $p$ and to the induced cocone $p_C:C\to B$. Naturality of the preceding construction gives its comparison as a map of spaces over the fixed $M=\operatorname{Map}_B(p_i(x),p_i(y))$. The coherent triangles $p_jD(u)\simeq p_i$ identify the two endpoints throughout $J$ with those at $i$; these identifications and their higher compatibilities, not strict equality of endpoints, specify the maps to $M$. By the fixed-object filtered-colimit clause applied in spaces, $\operatorname{colim}_J\Delta_J M\simeq M$. For the specified vertex $f\in M$, express each $\operatorname{Map}_{D_j}^f$ as $\operatorname{Map}_{D_j}\times_M^h\{f\}$. Space finite-limit exactness takes their filtered colimit to $(\operatorname{colim}_J\operatorname{Map}_{D_j})\times_M^h\{f\}$, which step 10 identifies over $M$ with $\operatorname{Map}_C^f$. All maps are induced by the given functors to $B$, and the natural simplicial mapping-space comparisons, so this also proves the asserted naturality under those functors. Nothing in the argument requires an injective map on objects or a fully faithful transition functor; the pullbacks are homotopy pullbacks throughout.
